paper text.text:
A combination cannot give $G$ if it has two disjoint twin
triples, three distinct twin triples sharing a pair,
or a bridge with four attachments for some choice of twin pairs.
These conditions remain when another form or $cd$ is added.
Only $a,b,c,d$ gain incident edges, and none can belong to a
twin pair. The vertices $a,b$ have degree at least four.
A vertex sharing the neighbors of $c$ would be adjacent to
both $p,q$, so would have to be $a$ or $b$, and similarly for
$d$. Thus every existing twin pair keeps its neighborhood,
and a component with four attachments remains inside a component
meeting the same four vertices. Also, a combination containing
a smaller nontoroidal combination has a proper nontoroidal minor.

The enumeration~\supp{E20} uses these

vertex names: Psi_2: twins p, q with neighbourhood {a,b,c} and r, z with neighbourhood {a,b,d}, as in Section 5. Further vertices with these neighbourhoods are p3, ... and r3, .... Interior vertices of bridges are u0, u1, ... Vertices of the k-th form are f<k>_<i>.
